cover.headline: The best growth story in Indian two-wheelers, priced as if it can only get better
cover.lead: TVS Motor has nearly doubled its volumes in five years (3.05mn vehicles in FY21, 5.89mn in FY26), lifted its domestic two-wheeler share from ~17.6% (FY24) to ~19.6% (FY26), leads India's electric two-wheeler market (24.3% in FY26, 27.1% in Aug-2026) and grew exports 31% last year. Q1FY27 was its best quarter: revenue +38%, EBITDA margin 12.8% despite a 3.5% commodity hit, profit +51%. The street values TVS as the standalone auto business on P/E plus TVS Credit on book; so do we: **25.5x Sep-28E standalone EPS** (its own 27.4x median one-year-forward P/E since 2021, cut by the 6.9% de-rating of auto peers) gives ₹3,025, TVS Credit at 2x book adds ₹329 and the loss-making subsidiaries (Norton, the Swiss e-bike group) take off ₹26. That is **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** At ₹4,106 the stock trades at 35.7x our FY28E EPS, near the top of its history. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The franchise is winning on every front that matters
arguments.p: Domestic ICE two-wheelers grew 19% in FY26 against 9% for the industry and 21% vs 13% in Q1FY27; TVS sold more two-wheelers than Hero or Honda (domestic plus exports) in June and August 2026. iQube and Orbiter made it #1 in EVs; HLX motorcycles crossed 5mn units in Africa and LatAm. We forecast {{F.volume.0|mn}}mn vehicles in FY27E (+18%) and EPS of {{F.eps.0|inr}} / {{F.eps.1|inr}} / {{F.eps.2|inr}} for FY27-29E.

arguments.h: But it is still a 13% margin business, and the PLI ends in FY28
arguments.p: EBITDA margin has sat at 12.5-13.1% for six quarters, below Hero (14.9%) and far below Bajaj (20.8%) and Eicher (24.7%). Roughly 0.6-0.9% of revenue is a production-linked incentive that the scheme stops paying after March 2028; we take it out of FY29E. Commodity inflation of ~4% of revenue in H1FY27 was offset, not reversed.

TVS put ~₹2,400 cr into subsidiaries in FY26 and guides ₹1,700-1,900 cr for FY27. Norton lost ₹723 cr and the Swiss e-bike group ₹417 cr in FY26; the subsidiaries other than TVS Credit lose ~₹1,300 cr a year (Q1FY27 run-rate unchanged). TVS Credit is the valuable one (ROE ~16%, July-2026 deal at 2.6x book) and a separation is being explored; we value TVS Motor's 85.6% at ₹329 a share.

arguments.h: The price assumes the premium is permanent
arguments.p: The street's 33-35x standalone P/E plus TVS Credit equals TVS Motor's own peak-period multiple, not its median. Our 25.5x needs no view on growth: it is the house method (median since 2021 × sector de-rating). Even the post-2023 median (31.8x) would leave the stock overvalued. Street targets ₹3,930-5,300 (median ₹4,265); ours is the lowest. Our DCF (₹2,845) and EV/EBITDA (₹3,837) cross-checks bracket the target.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026) and festive retail (October-November 2026): the first test of demand against the post-GST base from Q3.
TVS Credit separation: the chairman said at the July 2026 AGM that options including a separation are being evaluated "in stages"; TVS paid ₹711 cr for 4.39% on 27-Jul-2026.
Norton: four models launched in Europe and India in Q1FY27, US entry due in summer FY27; any volume and loss disclosure.
Capacity to 8.3mn two-wheelers and 0.42mn three-wheelers by Q4FY27; EV capacity 50k+ a month.
Policy: PM E-DRIVE e-2W subsidy (₹5,000 cap) runs to Mar-2028; auto PLI ends Mar-2028; draft Delhi proposal to stop ICE two-wheeler sales from 2028.

sections.title: A two-wheeler maker with four engines: domestic scooters and bikes, EVs, exports and a lender

blocks.p: India's third-largest two-wheeler maker and the world's third-largest by its own description: motorcycles (Apache, Raider, Ronin, HLX for exports, Sport, Radeon), scooters (Jupiter, Ntorq, Zest), the XL100 moped, electric scooters (iQube, Orbiter) and three-wheelers (King). sections.title: Two-wheelers are back above the 2019 peak; scooters, premium bikes and EVs lead

blocks.p: India's domestic two-wheeler market took seven years to get back to its FY19 peak of 21.2mn. It fell to 13.5mn in FY22 (BS-VI price increases, COVID, higher insurance costs) and recovered to 21.7mn in FY26, helped in H2 by the September-2025 GST cut. The mix changed on the way: scooters grew 18.5% in FY26 to 8.1mn while motorcycles grew 6.6% to 13.5mn, and premium motorcycles reached 1.83mn. Electric two-wheelers were ~6.5% of registrations in FY26 and 10.5-11.1% in Jul-Aug 2026.

blocks.h: What drives the next three years

bullets: **GST 2.0 (from 22-Sep-2025):** an ~8% price cut on bikes and scooters up to 350cc; bikes above 350cc moved to 40%. Industry H2FY26 growth was ~20%+; TVS passed the full cut to customers.

**FY27 so far:** TVS says the industry grew 13% (domestic ICE) in Q1 and will grow "double digits" in FY27; CRISIL (quoted in the AR) expected 7-9% including exports. From Q3FY27 the comparison base includes the GST jump.

**EVs:** PM E-DRIVE support was extended to Mar-2028 but is small (₹2,500/kWh, ₹5,000 cap). Rare-earth magnet curbs (from Apr-2025) showed the supply risk. A draft Delhi policy would stop ICE two-wheeler sales from 2028.
**Exports:** India shipped 4.2mn two-wheelers in FY25 (+22%); Africa recovered from its 2022-24 currency crises; TVS grew 31% in FY26 vs 12% for the industry.
**Headwinds:** commodity costs (3-5% of revenue in early FY27), an El Niño risk to rural incomes, and rising competition in EVs and 125cc+ scooters.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** few Indian companies are as well placed for the next three years of two-wheeler demand: scooters, EVs and exports are TVS's strongest areas and the fastest-growing parts of the market. The investment question is not whether TVS grows. It is how much of that growth is already in a price of ~36x next-year earnings.

sections.title: Domestic ICE: share up ~2 points in two years, led by scooters

blocks.p: Domestic petrol (ICE) two-wheelers, with domestic three-wheelers and spares, are ~64% of TVS revenue. Volumes rose from 3.25mn in FY25 to 3.87mn in FY26 (+19% against +9% for the industry) and 21% in Q1FY27 (industry 13%). Including EVs, TVS sold 42,43,524 two-wheelers in India in FY26, ~19.6% of the market on our estimate (17.6% in FY24), and 18.8% in March 2026 (Hero 28.0%, Honda 25.9%). In June and August 2026 TVS sold more two-wheelers than Hero or Honda when exports are included. Scooters are the engine: domestic scooter sales (incl. EV) rose 27% to 2.30mn in FY26; motorcycles rose 18% to 1.42mn; the XL100 moped, a category TVS has almost to itself, grew 4% to 0.52mn.

bullets: **Portfolio built around the customer, not the price point:** Jupiter 110/125 (JD Power IQS/APEAL leaders), Ntorq 125 and the 150cc "hyper-sport" Ntorq launched in FY26, Raider 125, Apache RTR/RR/RTX 300 and Ronin. A refresh every season (management: "something new every time").
**Pricing power in scooters:** on the Q1FY27 call UBS noted a major rival was discounting scooters heavily while TVS still gained share at a premium price.
**Clean channel:** dealers are cash-and-carry and carry under 25-30 days of stock, so dispatches track retail. Q1 retail and wholesale share both rose.
**What could stop it:** Honda's scooter dominance (Activa) and its pricing; EV cannibalisation of TVS's own Jupiter; an El Niño-hit rural market from H2FY27; the post-GST base from Q3FY27.

blocks.p: **Forecast.** We assume domestic ICE volumes +11% in FY27E (H1 ~+20% already visible; H2 +5% on the post-GST base), then +6% and +5%, and revenue per vehicle +5% in FY27E (1.5% price in Q1, 0.5% in Q2, premium mix) and +3% a year after. That gives domestic ICE, 3W and spares revenue of ₹35,116 cr in FY27E and ₹41,584 cr in FY29E.

sections.title: EVs: #1 in India with ~27% share, but competition is close and profits thin

blocks.p: TVS sold 11,000 electric scooters in FY22 and 3,71,387 in FY26; Q1FY27 alone was 1,29,940 (+86%) and July-August another 120,000. The iQube (1mn+ built) and, since August 2025, the cheaper Orbiter made TVS the largest electric two-wheeler seller in FY26 with 24.3% of registrations (Bajaj 20.6%, Ather 17.0%, Ola 11.7%, Hero Vida 10.3%), rising to 27.1% in August 2026. EV revenue was ~₹5,000 cr in FY26 (~11% of revenue) and ~₹1,780 cr in Q1FY27 (~13%).

blocks.h: Three things that limit what EVs are worth to TVS

bullets: **Profit:** management says EV contribution is "becoming better and better quarter after quarter" but gives no EV margin. Part of the economics is the auto PLI (TVS: ~0.6-0.9% of total revenue), which ends in March 2028, and the PM E-DRIVE subsidy is now small (₹2,500/kWh, capped at ₹5,000 a vehicle, to Mar-2028).
**Supply:** China's rare-earth magnet curbs (from Apr-2025) cut TVS EV dispatches from 28k in May-2025 to 14.4k in June-2025; volumes took until early 2026 to recover fully.

**Competition and cannibalisation:** Bajaj (22.7% in Aug-2026), Ather (15.9%) and Hero Vida (10.5%) are close, and every iQube sold may be a Jupiter not sold. The EV gain partly replaces ICE profit rather than adding to it.

blocks.p: **Forecast.** EV volumes 6,38,065 in FY27E (+72%: Q1 130k and Jul-Aug 120k reported; capacity moving from 40k to 50k+ a month), then +25% and +20%. Revenue per EV −2% in FY27E and −1% a year after (Orbiter V1, battery-as-a-service plans). EV revenue ₹8,418 cr in FY27E and ₹12,376 cr in FY29E (16.6% of revenue).

sections.title: Exports: a quarter of revenue and the clearest structural edge

blocks.p: International business (two- and three-wheelers shipped from India) sold 15,84,763 vehicles in FY26 (+33%) for revenue of ~₹11,280 cr, and 4,68,354 in Q1FY27 (+33%) for ₹3,634 cr, ~26% of revenue. The workhorse is the HLX commuter motorcycle (100-150cc), built for African taxi use, which crossed 5mn units in 13 years (the last 1mn in one year). Africa has recovered from its 2022-24 currency crises; Latin America and the Middle East are the new focus; Apache, Ronin, Raider and iQube/Orbiter are being added market by market. PT TVS in Indonesia (a subsidiary, 0.20mn units in FY26) supplies ASEAN scooters and is not in these numbers.

pair.title: Exports: 0.84mn (FY20) to ~2.4mn (FY29E)

blocks.p: **Three-wheelers.** TVS sold 219,060 three-wheelers in FY26 (+63% vs industry +28%) and 66,697 in Q1FY27 (+48%), ~72% of them exported (King, King Kargo). At home it is building a position in electric passenger and cargo three-wheelers (EV penetration of the category crossed 40% in Q1FY27), with a Hyundai co-development deal and capacity going from 0.25mn to 0.42mn a year. It is still only 3.7% of TVS units; Bajaj dominates the segment.

**Forecast.** Two-wheeler exports +23% in FY27E (Q1 +32%, Jul-Aug +28% reported), then +12% and +10%; three-wheelers +30%, +15%, +12%. Export revenue per vehicle +7% in FY27E (Q1FY27 ran at ~₹77,600 vs ₹71,200 in FY26: mix, rupee, three-wheelers) and +3% a year after. Export revenue ₹14,896 cr in FY27E and ₹19,562 cr in FY29E. Risks: African currencies, fuel prices after the West Asia conflict (some markets saw petrol up 50-60%), container lead times (+15% in Q4FY26).

sections.title: TVS Credit: a ₹32,000 cr lender earning ~16% ROE, worth ~₹329 a share to TVS Motor

blocks.p: TVS Credit Services is an NBFC that finances TVS two-wheelers and three-wheelers, used cars and tractors, consumer durables, and personal and gold loans, mostly for self-employed and new-to-credit borrowers in semi-urban and rural India (2.6 crore customers, ~62,000 touch points). In FY26 its book grew 15% to ₹30,639 cr, disbursements 26% to ₹33,018 cr, and profit 19% to ₹913 cr on net worth of ₹6,068 cr (ROE ~16.6%). In Q1FY27 the book reached ₹32,053 cr (+19%) and profit ₹208.5 cr (+15%); gross Stage 3 fell to 2.2% (3.0% a year earlier); capital adequacy 18.5% (Tier 1 16.2%).

blocks.p: TVS Motor's investment in TVS Motor (Singapore), the holding company for Norton, the Swiss/German/UK e-bike businesses, TVS Digital and Engines Engineering (Italy), rose from ₹5,195 cr to ₹7,172 cr in FY26 alone (US$222m added). Norton has absorbed over £250m since its purchase in FY21 and lost ₹723 cr in FY26; TVS EBike, which bought the Swiss E-Mobility Group and EGO Movement, lost ₹431 cr on CHF 56m of revenue in a European market with "excess inventory and excessive discounting". Together with the holding company, DriveX and Ultraviolette, the subsidiaries other than TVS Credit cost TVS shareholders ~₹1,350 cr in FY26, about ₹28 a share, and Q1FY27 was no better.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a strong product and execution edge, but no cost moat

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. TVS has clear strengths in products, EVs and exports, and it has out-executed the market for five years. What it does not have is a cost or pricing advantage that shows up in margins: it earns about half of Bajaj's EBITDA margin and less than Hero's.

verdicts: Pan-India dealer network built over decades; strongest in the south and in scooters; dealer stock kept under 30 days (cash-and-carry dealers).

The main reason TVS has gained share in every year since FY21.
Customers pay a premium over a discounting rival in scooters (Q1FY27 call); premium motorcycles ~47% of FY26 motorcycle sales (Emkay).
Earned, not structural: rivals can and do launch into the same segments.
EBITDA margin 12.9% vs Bajaj 20.8%, Eicher 24.7%, Hero 14.9% (FY26); material cost 71% of sales.
No cost advantage: TVS earns less per vehicle than Hero, Bajaj or Eicher.
#1 in e-2W registrations in FY26 (24.3%) and Aug-2026 (27.1%); 1mn+ iQube built; in-house software/connected platform.
Leadership in a market where Bajaj, Ather and Hero Vida are close behind; EV profits still thin.

A genuine edge in commuter bikes for emerging markets; Bajaj is the bigger exporter.

sections.title: Q1FY27: record quarter, a 10% beat on EBITDA, and July-August even stronger

blocks.p: Q1FY27 (reported 21-Jul-2026) was TVS's biggest quarter: 16,30,558 vehicles (+28%), revenue ₹13,896 cr (+38%), EBITDA ₹1,779 cr (+41%) at a 12.8% margin (12.5% a year earlier), and profit ₹1,174 cr (+51%). sections.title: What you buy, what you pay, and what would change our mind

exhibit.title: The honest summary
head: Question
Answer
rows: India's best-executing two-wheeler maker: share gains every year since FY21, #1 in EVs, a fast-growing export business, ~86% of a 16%-ROE lender. Also a set of overseas subsidiaries that lose ~₹1,300 cr a year.
₹4,106: 35.7x our FY28E standalone EPS (median since 2021: 27.4x), ~49x trailing standalone EPS (twelve months to Jun-26) and ~65x FY26 consolidated EPS (₹63.5).
That ~20% EPS growth lasts well beyond FY28 and that the market keeps paying a peak multiple; that TVS Credit is worth ~2x book and Norton costs nothing.
{{dcf.tp|inr}} = 25.5x Sep-28E standalone EPS (₹3,025) + TVS Credit at 2x book (₹329) − other subsidiaries (₹26).

**SELL** ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%. At our target, the stock would be a BUY below ₹2,900 and a SELL above ₹3,510.
exhibit.source: GAM Research

blocks.h: Risks to our SELL (what could make the stock go up)

bullets: **Growth stays at 20%+ for longer:** if FY28-29E volumes grow 15% rather than 8-10% and margins reach 14%, EPS would be ~15% above ours; our bull case ({{scen.bull.tp|inr}}) roughly matches today's price.
**TVS Credit separation:** a listing at the July-2026 deal multiple (2.6x book) would show ~₹427 a share; at a market premium it could be more.
**Norton works:** if the four new models sell well in Europe, India and the US, the subsidiary losses could fall faster than we assume and Norton could be worth something.
**PLI renewal or a new EV incentive** would keep ~0.6-0.9% of revenue in the margin after FY28 (~+5% to FY29E EPS).
**The premium persists:** quality compounders in India have kept high multiples for long periods; TVS traded at 37x+ forward in FY17-20.

blocks.h: Risks to the business (what could make it worse than our base)

bullets: **Demand after the GST bump:** from Q3FY27 the comparison base includes the post-GST surge; an El Niño year could hit rural demand.
**Margins:** commodity costs (3-5% of revenue in H1FY27) and EV price competition; the PLI ends in Mar-2028.
**Capital allocation:** more money into Norton, e-bikes or new ventures (management: "some new investments will be there").
**EV policy and supply:** subsidies are small and time-bound; rare-earth magnets remain a single-country supply risk; a Delhi ICE ban would favour EV leaders but disrupt ICE volumes.
**Credit cycle at TVS Credit:** ~4% credit cost on a largely unsecured book; a downturn would hit both the lender and TVS sales.

blocks.callout: **How we would act.** At ₹4,106 we would sell or underweight: the business is excellent but the price already discounts several years of outperformance and ignores the subsidiary drag. We would turn more positive on (1) a price nearer ₹2,900, (2) evidence that Norton and the e-bike group are cutting losses, or (3) a clean separation of TVS Credit that returns its value to shareholders.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for TVS Motor Company, STANDALONE auto business (INR crore). Base year FY26A from Screener standalone. TVS Credit Services (85.6% after the Jul-2026 purchase) and the other subsidiaries (Norton, TVS EBike, DriveX, PT TVS Indonesia, DMCC, Ultraviolette) are valued separately in the sum of the parts (tools/authoring/TVSMOTOR.ctx.js); TVSMOTOR.sotp.js carries the SOTP into the engine as an implied multiple of standalone Sep-28E EPS.

volume._why: Sum of the segment build in businessLines (2W + 3W, domestic + exports). FY27E: Q1 1.63mn (+28%) and Jul-Aug 1.25mn (+29%) already reported; H2 assumed +8% on the GST-boosted H2FY26 base (3.10mn). FY28-29E: domestic ICE +6%/+5%, EV +25%/+20%, exports +12%/+10%, 3W +15%/+12%, within the 8.3mn 2W / 0.42mn 3W capacity due by Q4FY27.

assumptions._revPerUnitWhy: From the segment build: FY27E price hikes (~1.5% in Q1, ~0.5% in Q2), EV mix (9% of units vs 6%) and a firmer export realisation (Q1FY27 ₹77.6k vs FY26 ₹71.2k); Q1FY27 revenue per vehicle was already ₹85.2k (+8% YoY). FY28E ~3% (price ~2% + premium/EV mix). FY29E lower (+2.3%) because the auto PLI scheme ends on 31-Mar-2028 (≈0.6% of revenue).

businessLines._why: Volume x realisation build (units '000; realisation ₹ per vehicle). FY26 realisations: exports = international business revenue ₹11,280 cr (Q1-Q4FY26 calls: 2,487 + 2,885 + 2,909 + 2,999) ÷ 1,584.8k units; EV = ~₹5,000 cr (Q4FY26 call) ÷ 371.4k; domestic ICE 2W + domestic 3W = residual after government incentives (₹973.6 cr, AR FY26 note 21), incl. domestic spares. Checked against model revenue in TVSMOTOR.ctx.js.
businessLines._segWhy: Domestic ICE 2W: Q1FY27 +20%, Jul-Aug +19%; H2 +5% on the post-GST base → +11%; then industry ~5-6% plus share gains, less EV cannibalisation. EV: Q1 130k (+86%), Jul-Aug 120k; capacity moving to 50k+/month → ~638k (+72%), then +25%/+20% as penetration (10.5% in Aug-2026) rises. Exports 2W: Q1 +32%, Jul-Aug +28%; H2 +15% → +23%. 3W: capacity 0.25 → 0.42mn; Q1 +48%. Realisation: domestic +5% (price + premium mix), EV −2% (Orbiter V1, battery-as-a-service lowers ticket size), exports +7% (Q1 run-rate, rupee).

assumptions._marginWhy: FY27E 12.9%: Q1 12.8% absorbed ~3.5% commodity inflation (West Asia conflict) with ~1.5% price and cost cuts; a further ~0.5% commodity hit and ~0.5% price in Q2; operating leverage and better EV contribution. FY28E 13.2%: scale on the 8.3mn capacity, EV contribution rising. FY29E 12.9%: the auto PLI (≈0.6-0.7% of revenue, 0.9% in Q4FY26) ends after FY28 under the Mar-2028 scheme end; we do not assume a renewal.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guided ~₹3,500 cr (Q4FY26 call: ~₹2,000 cr products/R&D + ₹1,000 cr+ for 1.5mn extra capacity); we hold ~₹3,000 cr thereafter (R&D ₹1,254 cr in FY26 and rising). Excludes ₹1,700-1,900 cr a year of investments in subsidiaries (valued in the SOTP).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹901 cr on average gross block ₹10,769 cr = 8.4%; 8.2% because the engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP held flat). Gives FY27E ~₹1,100 cr vs Q1FY27 run-rate ₹1,060 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Standalone 'treasury' (cash + investments − borrowings) is mostly ₹11,349 cr of investments in subsidiaries at cost (TVS Motor Singapore ₹7,172 cr, TVS Credit ₹2,515 cr, DMCC ₹511 cr, PT TVS ₹477 cr, DriveX ₹314 cr...) that earn no income in the standalone P&L, less ₹3,733 cr of borrowings incl. ₹1,899 cr NCRPS. So no yield is applied; other income is built line by line below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 note 22 (standalone other income −₹30.0 cr): interest ₹34.6 cr + profit on sale of PPE ₹14.9 cr + sale of investments ₹2.1 cr + other non-operating ₹6.2 cr = ₹57.9 cr recurring, less fair-value losses ₹87.8 cr. FY27E = Q1's booked fair-value gain ₹150 cr + ~₹45 cr recurring for the rest of the year; FY28-29E recurring only (fair-value changes not forecast). TTM to Jun-26 (Screener) ₹45 cr: the swing is fair-value marks.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹204 cr incl. ~₹66 cr of the 6% NCRPS coupon (allotted 1-Sep-2025). Q1FY27 ₹76 cr (NCRPS ~₹28 cr). NCRPS redeemed 1-Sep-2026 (₹1,900 cr), so ~₹47 cr of coupon in FY27E; other borrowings rise to fund capex and subsidiaries (₹500 cr NCD mentioned on the Q1 call).
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 interim dividend ₹12/share (₹570 cr, 16% of PAT); the ₹1,900 cr NCRPS bonus (₹40/share, redeemed Sep-2026) was a one-off capital return.

dcf._why: Cost of equity 6.5% + 0.95 x 6% = 12.2%; standalone net debt is small, so WACC = Ke. 15 years: revenue growth fades from FY29E's ~11% to 9% (volume ~5% + price/mix ~4%), EBITDA margin to 13.5%, capex to 4% of revenue; terminal growth 6%. Net cash in the engine includes subsidiaries at cost (₹239/share), so the DCF compares with the whole SOTP.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Domestic share keeps rising (TVS was India's #1 2W seller by total volume in Jun-Aug 2026), EV penetration passes 15% with TVS holding ~27%, exports grow 20%+ a year, PLI is renewed; TVS Credit is separated at the July-2026 deal multiple and Norton finds buyers.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The GST-led demand fades from Q3FY27 on a high base and El Niño, commodity costs stay high, EV competition (Bajaj, Ather, Hero Vida) caps share and price, PLI ends; Norton and TVS EBike keep losing ~₹1,300 cr a year beyond FY29.

methods.name: SOTP (standalone P/E + TVS Credit P/B + other subsidiaries)
methods.why: How the street values TVS Motor: standalone P/E plus TVS Credit on P/B (PL 35x FY28E + ₹93; BOBCAPS 33x Jun-28E + ₹133; Nirmal Bang 34x Jun-28E + 1.5x book; Choice 34x FY28E + ₹101; Axis core P/E + 1.5x book + other investments; Emkay 35x Jun-28E + 2x book; Jul-Aug 2026). The engine cannot add parts to a P/E, so this multiple is the SOTP value per share divided by standalone Sep-28E EPS, written by TVSMOTOR.sotp.js. The parts and the derivation of each multiple are in the valuation chapter.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash (incl. subsidiaries at cost) at face value. 17.8x Sep-28E EBITDA = TVS Motor's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 less the same sector de-rating, restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being above the twelve months to Jun-26; bull/bear scale with the P/E multiples. Derived in TVSMOTOR.ctx.js.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests cash-flow support: 15-year FCFF of the standalone business, Ke 12.2%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash (which includes subsidiaries at cost).
